question_text: If x = cos θ + i sin θ, then find x⁶ + 1/x⁶.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this — what De Moivre gives for x⁶, what its reciprocal is, and what their sum is.
insider_note: The second mark depends on |x| = 1: only then is 1/x⁶ the conjugate of x⁶, so the sines cancel. The answer is 2cos 6θ — a stray i means the two were subtracted, and 2cos⁶ θ means the power was left on the cosine instead of the angle.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: x⁶ and 1/x⁶ by De Moivre
steps.margin_note: First mark. x⁶ = cos 6θ + i sin 6θ by De Moivre. Since |x| = 1, the reciprocal is the conjugate, so 1/x⁶ = cos 6θ − i sin 6θ.
lines: x⁶ = (cos θ + i sin θ)⁶ = cos 6θ + i sin 6θ

recall.must_convey: That x⁶ = cos 6θ + i sin 6θ by De Moivre's theorem and 1/x⁶ is the conjugate cos 6θ − i sin 6θ.
accept: x to the six is cos six theta plus i sin six theta by De Moivre and one by x to the six is cos six theta minus i sin six theta
raise to six so the angle becomes six theta, and the reciprocal has minus i sin
De Moivre gives cis six theta and the reciprocal is cis minus six theta
De Moivre tho x power six cis six theta, reciprocal lo sin sign minus
the sixth power multiplies the angle by six and the reciprocal is its conjugate

steps.why: De Moivre puts the 6 onto the angle. Since |x| = 1, the reciprocal of x⁶ is its conjugate, so the two terms differ only in the sign of the sine.
common_mistakes: Writing x⁶ = cos⁶ θ + i sin⁶ θ.
Writing 1/x⁶ = cos 6θ + i sin 6θ with no sign change.
Trying to find 1/x⁶ by rationalising a six-fold product.

steps.label: Add
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Adding the two cancels the sines and doubles the cosine: x⁶ + 1/x⁶ = 2cos 6θ. No i is left, and the angle stays 6θ.

recall.must_convey: That the reduced expression is evaluated to 2cos 6θ.
accept: evaluate the reduced form and get 2cos 6θ
simplify the powers of omega and the value is 2cos 6θ

steps.why: A number of modulus 1 plus its conjugate is twice the real part. The sines cancel and the cosines double.
common_mistakes: Writing 2i sin 6θ, the difference instead of the sum.
Leaving a stray i in the answer.
